title: AI Foundations — Intermediate Applied Practical Exam
instructions: This course uses a structured, text-submission practical assessment. The current runner checks defined expected outputs and required reasoning elements; it does not execute submitted code. Submit your own analysis for each scenario.

tasks.title: Calculate and report classification metrics
tasks.prompt: A binary classifier was evaluated on a held-out test set of 100 examples. Its confusion-matrix counts are TP=45, FP=15, FN=5, and TN=35. The positive class is the target class. Calculate accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. Submit only a JSON object with numeric values rounded to four decimal places, using ratios rather than percentage values. Use exactly these keys: accuracy, precision, recall, f1.
rubric: Compute metrics from the supplied confusion matrix, not from training-set performance.
Use accuracy=(TP+TN)/(TP+FP+FN+TN), precision=TP/(TP+FP), recall=TP/(TP+FN), and F1=2×precision×recall/(precision+recall).
Return valid JSON with the four requested numeric fields, rounded to four decimal places.

tasks.title: Repair a leaking data preparation workflow
tasks.prompt: A binary classification dataset has repeated patient IDs; some records for the same patient appear in both training and test data. A scaler and missing-value imputer were fitted on the full dataset before splitting. Describe a corrected evaluation workflow, including how you prevent leakage and establish a meaningful comparison. Include these exact phrases in your answer: data leakage, train/test split, validation set, fit only on training data, baseline.

Diagnosis:

Corrected workflow:

How the result will be evaluated:
rubric: Identify the duplicate-entity overlap and preprocessing-before-split as sources of data leakage.
Split by patient or another appropriate grouping so one entity cannot cross the train/test boundary.
Fit imputers, scalers, feature selection, and other learned preprocessing only on training data; use a validation set for tuning and keep the test set held out.
Compare against a simple baseline using appropriate metrics.

tasks.prompt: Design a support assistant that answers questions from a private collection of policy documents. Explain how it should retrieve evidence, communicate uncertainty, and behave when a request is malicious or the documents do not support an answer. Include these exact phrases in your response: retrieval, citations, prompt injection, untrusted input, privacy, fallback.

rubric: Ground responses in retrieved policy content and provide citations or source references.
Treat retrieved documents and user content as untrusted input; explicitly mitigate prompt injection.
Avoid exposing private information and define a safe fallback or human-escalation path when evidence is missing.
